Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future closed null cone is
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $\nabla$ be an affine connection on
$M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) and let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, with Christoffel symbols $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a
\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$ ([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]])
and metric components $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$. Then:

1. $\nabla$ is torsion-free ([[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]])
   if and only if $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\Gamma^a{}_{cb}$ for all $a,b,c$ in every
   smooth chart.
2. $\nabla$ is $g$-compatible ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) if and
   only if, in every smooth chart,

$$\partial_ag_{bc}=\sum_{d=0}^{3}\bigl(\Gamma^d{}_{ab}g_{dc}+\Gamma^d{}_{ac}g_{bd}\bigr) \qquad(a,b,c=0,1,2,3).$$

Thus $\nabla$ is metric-selected for $(M,g)$ if and only if both displayed
conditions hold in every smooth chart.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.


**(d) Intrinsic construction before physical use.** For smooth local vector
fields define the Koszul expression

$$K(X,Y,Z):=Xg(Y,Z)+Yg(Z,X)-Zg(X,Y)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X).$$

Define $\nabla^g_XY$ by $2g(\nabla^g_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)$ for every smooth local
$Z$. The proof below establishes existence, smoothness, the affine-connection
rules, metric compatibility, torsion freedom and uniqueness; it uses symmetry
and nondegeneracy, not positive definiteness. Thus $\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$
has this unique element, called the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$. The later
nondegenerate-metric theorem retains its fuller tensor-derivative statement.
Its Christoffel symbols in any chart are defined by
$\nabla^g_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) and obey

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12 g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}),\qquad a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3.$$

**(e) Basic curvature and contractions.** The **curvature** of this connection
is the operator of [[def-curvature-of-an-affine-connection]], with the fixed
sign convention

$$R^g(X,Y)Z:=\nabla^g_X\nabla^g_YZ-\nabla^g_Y\nabla^g_XZ-\nabla^g_{[X,Y]}Z.$$

The general affine-connection theorem
[[thm-curvature-is-a-type-one-three-tensor]] proves that it depends pointwise
only on $X,Y,Z$ and is a smooth tensor. Define its chart components by
$R^g(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$.
Define the **Ricci tensor** and **scalar curvature** pointwise by

$$\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,w):=\operatorname{tr}(z\mapsto R^g_p(z,w)v),\qquad S(p):=\operatorname{tr}(\sharp_p\circ\operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p),\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p(v):=\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,\cdot).$$

Here $\sharp$ is the inverse metric isomorphism and traces are the
basis-independent trace of [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Equivalently,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\sum_aR^a{}_{bad}$ and
$S=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}$, all sums from $0$ through $3$.
These are well-defined smooth fields by finite contraction of the smooth
components of $R^g$ and $g^{-1}$; basis independence follows from the trace
and the intrinsic maps just defined. No symmetry identity or field equation
is assumed here. Lowering the curvature output gives
$R_{abcd}=g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd}$, so the definitions agree with the full later
curvature item, which proves the remaining symmetries and coordinate formulas.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on the tensor bundles
of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

In coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^n$, a smooth curve $\gamma$ is a geodesic if and only if, throughout every parameter subinterval lying in the chart,
$$\ddot x^k+\Gamma^k{}_{ij}(x)\dot x^i\dot x^j=0\qquad(1\le k\le n),$$
with summation over repeated indices.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold without boundary with affine connection $\nabla$, and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior. A smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ is an **affinely parametrized geodesic** when
$$D_t\gamma'(t)=0\qquad(t\in I),$$
with one-sided interpretation at an included endpoint. Constant curves are geodesics. Unless another parametrization is explicitly stated, “geodesic” means affinely parametrized geodesic.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ and the chart $x=\psi_p$ on $T_0M$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.

For a given connection on $E$ and a smooth curve on an interval with nonempty interior, the **covariant derivative along the curve** is
$$D_tV=(\gamma^*\nabla)_{\partial/\partial t}V.$$
Here $V$ is a section of the pullback bundle as in [[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]], and the pullback connection exists by [[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. It is real-linear and satisfies $D_t(fV)=f'V+fD_tV$ for functions of the parameter.

At an included endpoint the smooth up-to-boundary coefficients have their one-sided derivative; equivalently any smooth local extension of the coefficients gives this value, because extensions agreeing on a one-sided interval have the same derivative there. For a piecewise smooth curve the derivative is defined on each piece, with separate one-sided derivatives at corners; those derivatives are not required to agree. A singleton interval carries no derivative operator under this convention and will have identity transport by definition. A zero section or a rank-zero bundle gives zero covariant derivative. Constant base curves can have sections with nonzero coefficient derivative.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$ be its curvature ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be an affinely parametrized
geodesic with $D_s\gamma'=0$, written $T:=\gamma'$
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]); the parameter is the affinely
parametrized one of that definition and need not be proper time.

**(a) Fields along $\gamma$ and the derivative $D_s$.** A **field along
$\gamma$** is a section $J$ of the pullback bundle $\gamma^*TM$, and $D_s$
denotes the covariant derivative along $\gamma$ of
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]. A field is **smooth** when its
coefficients in a smooth local frame of $M$ around each point of $\gamma$ are
$C^\infty$ on the corresponding parameter interval. At an included endpoint
of $I$ all derivatives below are one-sided.

**(b) Jacobi field.** A **Jacobi field along $\gamma$** is a smooth field $J$
along $\gamma$ satisfying the **Jacobi equation**
$$D_s^2J=R(T,J)T\qquad(s\in I),$$
that is $D_s^2J=R(\gamma',J)\gamma'$. The assignment
$J\mapsto R(T,J)T$, which associates with a field along $\gamma$ another
field along $\gamma$ and is $\mathbb R$-linear, is the **Jacobi operator of
$\gamma$**. Whether the field is smooth only piecewise is stated whenever a
statement uses piecewise fields; the unqualified term means globally smooth.

**(c) Geodesic variations.** A **geodesic variation with affine
parameter $s$** is a smooth map $F:J_0\times I\to M$, where
$J_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an open interval with nonempty interior, such that
for every $r\in J_0$ the curve $s\mapsto F(r,s)$ is a geodesic with affine
parameter $s$. Its **variation field** is the field $s\mapsto\partial_rF(r,s)$
along the curve $s\mapsto F(0,s)$. The variation field of a geodesic
variation is a Jacobi field along that curve
([[thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-deviation]] clause (c)).

**(d) Conjugate instants and multiplicity.** Let $s_0<s_1$ be points of $I$.
The event $\gamma(s_1)$ is **conjugate to** $\gamma(s_0)$ **along $\gamma$**
when there is a nonzero Jacobi field $J$ along $\gamma$ with
$J(s_0)=J(s_1)=0$. In that case $s_1$ is called a **conjugate instant** of
$\gamma$ (with respect to $s_0$, when the base point needs to be named), and
the **multiplicity** of the conjugate instant is the dimension of the real
vector space of Jacobi fields vanishing at $s_0$ and $s_1$; the fields
vanishing at $s_0$ form a $4$-dimensional space and the multiplicity is at
most $4$, since a Jacobi field is determined by its value and derivative at
$s_0$ ([[thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-deviation]] clause (d)). For a
geodesic with $\gamma(s_0)=p$ and $\gamma'(s_0)=v$, the corresponding
possibility of conjugacy is measured by the derivative of the exponential
map at $s_1v$
([[lem-gr-conjugacy-via-the-exponential-map]]); that equivalence is proved,
not assumed here. No conjugate instant is asserted to exist.

**(e) The normal bundle.** If $\gamma$ is future timelike with
$g(T,T)=-1$, define its **normal bundle** to be the vector subbundle
$$N_\gamma:=\bigsqcup_{s\in I}N_\gamma(s)\subseteq\gamma^*TM,\qquad N_\gamma(s):=\{v\in T_{\gamma(s)}M:g_{\gamma(s)}(v,T(s))=0\}.$$
A **normal field** is a smooth section $J$ of $N_\gamma$, equivalently a
smooth field along $\gamma$ satisfying $g(J,T)=0$. Each fibre $N_\gamma(s)$
has dimension three, the restriction of $g_{\gamma(s)}$ to it is positive
definite, and $D_s$ maps normal fields to normal fields, since
$\frac{d}{ds}g(J,T)=g(D_sJ,T)+g(J,D_sT)=g(D_sJ,T)$ and $D_sT=0$; these
facts are proved in [[lem-gr-normal-index-form-factorization]] clause (b).
The norm of a normal field is $|J(s)|:=\sqrt{g_{\gamma(s)}(J(s),J(s))}$.
For any field $V$ along $\gamma$, its **normal component** is the field
$$V^\perp(s):=V(s)+g_{\gamma(s)}(V(s),T(s))\,T(s).$$
Indeed $g(T,T)=-1$ implies $g(V^\perp,T)=0$ and
$V=V^\perp-g(V,T)T$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $R$ be its
curvature ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let
$I,J_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be intervals with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]), and let $F:J_0\times I\to M$ be a smooth map. Write
$T:=\partial_tF$ and $J^F:=\partial_rF$; a field along $F$ means a smooth
section of $F^*TM$ over $J_0\times I$, and $D_r,D_t$ are the covariant
derivatives in the two parameters
([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Curvature as the commutator of the two derivatives.** For every smooth
field $V$ along $F$,
$$\bigl(D_tD_r-D_rD_t\bigr)V=R(T,J^F)V .$$

**(b) Geodesic deviation.** Suppose in addition that for every $r\in J_0$ the
curve $t\mapsto F(r,t)$ is a geodesic with affine parameter $t$, that is
$D_tT=0$. Then $D_tJ^F=D_rT$ and
$$D_t^2J^F=R(T,J^F)T .$$
Consequently, for every $r$ the field $t\mapsto J^F(r,t)$ is a Jacobi field
along the geodesic $t\mapsto F(r,t)$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (b)), and for a geodesic
variation the variation field is a Jacobi field.

**(c) Initial data.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a smooth geodesic and let
$s_0\in I$. For every pair $J_0,J_1\in T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$ there exists exactly
one smooth Jacobi field $J$ along $\gamma$ with
$$J(s_0)=J_0,\qquad D_sJ(s_0)=J_1 .$$
The set of all Jacobi fields along $\gamma$ is a real vector space of
dimension $8$, and $J\mapsto\bigl(J(s_0),D_sJ(s_0)\bigr)$ is a linear
isomorphism onto $T_{\gamma(s_0)}M\oplus T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$.

**(d) The tangential component.** Let $\gamma$ be a smooth geodesic and $J$ a
smooth Jacobi field along it. Then $s\mapsto g(J,\gamma')(s)$ is affine, and
if $\gamma$ is future timelike with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-1$, the normal
component $J^\perp$ of [[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause
(e), explicitly $J^\perp=J+g(J,\gamma')\gamma'$, is again a Jacobi field
along $\gamma$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $p\in M$,
let $\mathcal E_p\subseteq T_pM$ be the exponential domain and
$\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$ the exponential map of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]], and identify
$T_{h}(T_pM)$ with $T_pM$ by the canonical isomorphism for every
$h\in T_pM$ ([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]).

**(a) The differential in terms of Jacobi fields.** Let $v\in T_pM$, let
$s_1>0$ satisfy $s_1v\in\mathcal E_p$, and let $u\in T_pM$. Let
$\gamma:[0,s_1]\to M$, $\gamma(t):=\exp_p(tv)$ (well defined by star-shapedness
of $\mathcal E_p$), and let $J_u$ be the unique Jacobi field along
$\gamma$ with $J_u(0)=0$ and $D_tJ_u(0)=u$
([[thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-deviation]] clause (c),
[[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (b)). Then
$$d(\exp_p)_{tv}(tu)=J_u(t)\qquad(0\le t\le s_1);$$
in particular $d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}(s_1u)=J_u(s_1)$ and, in the special case
$s_1=1$, $v\in\mathcal E_p$, $d(\exp_p)_v(u)=J_u(1)$.

**(b) Conjugacy as a kernel condition.** With the notation of (a),
$d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}$ is injective if and only if no nonzero Jacobi field
along $\gamma$ vanishes at $t=0$ and at $t=s_1$. Moreover
$\ker d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}=s_1\{u\in T_pM:J_u(s_1)=0\}$, so
$\dim\ker d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}$ equals the multiplicity of the conjugate
instant $s_1$ whenever $\gamma(s_1)$ is conjugate to $p$ along $\gamma$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (d)).

**(c) Conjugate instants of a geodesic.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a smooth
geodesic with $\gamma(0)=p$, and let $s_1>0$ with $s_1\in I$ and
$s_1\gamma'(0)\in\mathcal E_p$. Then $\gamma(s_1)$ is conjugate to
$\gamma(0)=p$ along $\gamma$ if and only if $d(\exp_p)_{s_1\gamma'(0)}$ is
not injective.

derivations.claim: (The metric-selected connection and its geodesics.) For the coordinate connection with $\Gamma\equiv0$ the symmetry $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\Gamma^a{}_{cb}$ is immediate and the compatibility identity of [L2] reads $\partial_ag_{bc}=0$, which holds because the metric components are constant; hence by [L2] this connection is the metric-selected connection and unique. By [L3] its geodesic equation is $\ddot x^k=0$, whose solutions are the affine lines, so the maximal geodesic with initial data $(p,v)$ is $t\mapsto p+tv$ defined on all of $\mathbb R$; therefore $\exp_p(v)=p+v$, and differentiating the chart expression of this translation gives $d(\exp_p)_u=\operatorname{id}$ for every $u$.

(Vanishing curvature and the componentwise derivative.) With $\Gamma\equiv0$ every term of the coordinate formula [L4] contains a Christoffel symbol or a derivative of one, so $R^a{}_{bcd}=0$ for all $a,b,c,d$ and $R=0$. By [L5], for a field $V=\sum_aV^a\partial_a$ along a curve, $D_tV=\sum_a(\partial_tV^a)\partial_a$: the identity frame is parallel along every curve, and $D_t$ is the componentwise derivative.

(Jacobi fields are affine.) Let $J=\sum_aJ^a\partial_a$ be a smooth field along the geodesic $\gamma(t)=p+tv$; by step 1.1 $\gamma'=v$ has constant components. By step 1.2, $D_t^2J=\sum_a(J^a)''\partial_a$ and $R(\gamma',J)\gamma'=0$, so the Jacobi equation of [L6] is equivalent to $(J^a)''=0$ for $a=0,1,2,3$, whose solutions are exactly the affine functions $J^a(t)=J^a_0+tJ^a_1$. Hence the Jacobi fields are exactly the fields $J(t)=J_0+tJ_1$ with $J_0,J_1\in\mathbb R^4$, and $D_tJ(0)=J_1$ by step 1.2.

(No conjugate instants.) Let $t_0<t_1$ and let $J(t)=J_0+tJ_1$ be a Jacobi field as in step 2.1. If $J(t_0)=J(t_1)=0$, then subtracting the two equations gives $(t_1-t_0)J_1=0$, so $J_1=0$, and then $J_0=J(t_0)=0$: the only Jacobi field vanishing at two instants is the zero field. By [L7] applied to the geodesic $\gamma(t)=\exp_p(tv)$, whose exponential data lie in the domain $T_pM$ by step 1.1, $d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}$ is injective for every $s_1>0$ and every $v$: no geodesic of the flat model has a conjugate instant relative to any of its points.

(The flat congruence.) Let $F(t,r):=p+tv+rw$ and $T=\partial_tF=v$, $J=\partial_rF=w$, both with constant components. By step 1.2, $D_t^2J=0$ and $R(T,J)T=0$, so $D_t^2J=R(T,J)T$ holds, in accordance with the deviation equation of [L6]; the variation field is parallel and the relative acceleration of the family vanishes everywhere.

boundaries.reason: No family or aggregate is quantified: the example fixes one flat metric, one geodesic gamma(t) = p + tv and one congruence F, and the arguments are pointwise in the parameter.

boundaries.evidence: Step 3.1 divides by the difference t1 - t0 when two zeros are subtracted; the hypothesis t0 < t1 makes the divisor nonzero, and step 4.1's constant variation field allows J = 0 without any division.

The one-dimensional reduction is explicit: step 2.1 reduces the Jacobi equation to four scalar equations (J^a)'' = 0, so the base case of a single component is solved and then assembled into the vector solution.

Degenerate data are included: step 1.1 allows v = 0, in which case the 'geodesic' is the constant curve and step 2.1's affine solutions still hold; step 4.1's congruence allows w = 0 and then J = 0 identically.

boundaries.reason: The geodesics are defined on all of R and the statements are pointwise, so no included endpoint or one-sided derivative appears in steps 1.1-4.1.

The identity chart is given, the connection is computed on it, and the parallel frame in step 1.2 is the coordinate frame itself; nothing is selected from a family, so no choice principle is involved.
The example states equalities and a nonexistence claim, not a biconditional; no forward implication between conditions is asserted.
No converse is claimed, so there is no reverse direction; step 3.1 completes the conjugate-instant argument.

Let $S^2:=\{(X,Y,Z)\in\mathbb R^3:X^2+Y^2+Z^2=1\}$ with the round metric
induced by the Euclidean inner product, and let $M:=\mathbb R^2\times S^2$
with the product Lorentzian metric whose first factor has line element
$-(dx^0)^2+(dx^3)^2$. Use the sphere chart
$\sigma:(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)\to S^2$ given by
$$\sigma(\theta,\varphi)=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta),$$
and put $U:=\mathbb R^2\times\sigma((0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi))\subset M$. In the
product chart with coordinate order
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(x^0,\theta,\varphi,x^3)$, the metric is
$$g:=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+\sin^2(x^1)\,(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2,\qquad N:=\partial_0 .$$
This chart contains the equatorial geodesic segment used in
[[ex-gr-conjugate-instant-on-a-round-sphere-factor]]; the underlying manifold
has an actual $S^2$ factor, not an unwrapped angular cover. The metric is
smooth and Lorentzian on $M$ with time orientation $N$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected
connection and $R$, $R_{abcd}$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ its curvature data
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Then:

1. The only nonzero Christoffel symbols in this chart are
   $$\Gamma^1{}_{22}=-\sin x^1\cos x^1,\qquad \Gamma^2{}_{12}=\Gamma^2{}_{21}=\cot x^1 .$$
2. The curvature has exactly one independent nonzero lowered component up
   to the algebraic symmetries, namely
   $$R_{1212}=\sin^2(x^1);$$ equivalently $R(\partial_1,\partial_2)\partial_2=\sin^2(x^1)\partial_1$ and $R(\partial_1,\partial_2)\partial_1=-\partial_2$, and every component containing an index $0$ or $3$ vanishes.
3. The Ricci tensor, scalar curvature and Einstein tensor are $$\operatorname{Ric}_{11}=1,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{22}=\sin^2(x^1),\qquad S=2,\qquad G=\operatorname{diag}(1,0,0,-1).$$
4. The contracted second Bianchi identity $\nabla^aG_{ab}=0$ holds. In the
   displayed chart $U$, $\nabla_eG_{ab}=0$ identically, so the divergence
   vanishes term by term there.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold without boundary with affine connection $\nabla$, and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior. A smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ is an **affinely parametrized geodesic** when
$$D_t\gamma'(t)=0\qquad(t\in I),$$
with one-sided interpretation at an included endpoint. Constant curves are geodesics. Unless another parametrization is explicitly stated, “geodesic” means affinely parametrized geodesic.

For a given connection on $E$ and a smooth curve on an interval with nonempty interior, the **covariant derivative along the curve** is
$$D_tV=(\gamma^*\nabla)_{\partial/\partial t}V.$$
Here $V$ is a section of the pullback bundle as in [[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]], and the pullback connection exists by [[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. It is real-linear and satisfies $D_t(fV)=f'V+fD_tV$ for functions of the parameter.

At an included endpoint the smooth up-to-boundary coefficients have their one-sided derivative; equivalently any smooth local extension of the coefficients gives this value, because extensions agreeing on a one-sided interval have the same derivative there. For a piecewise smooth curve the derivative is defined on each piece, with separate one-sided derivatives at corners; those derivatives are not required to agree. A singleton interval carries no derivative operator under this convention and will have identity transport by definition. A zero section or a rank-zero bundle gives zero covariant derivative. Constant base curves can have sections with nonzero coefficient derivative.

For an affine connection as in [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]] and coordinates $(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, its **Christoffel symbols** in this chart are the unique smooth functions $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ such that
$$\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j=\sum_k\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k.$$
The first lower index $i$ is the differentiating direction and the second lower index $j$ labels the differentiated vector field. In the coordinate frame, the one-forms from [[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]] are $\omega^k{}_j=\sum_i\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\,dx^i$. A different chart generally has different symbols. This definition asserts neither symmetry in $i,j$ nor tensorial transformation.

For dimension one there is one smooth coefficient $\Gamma^1{}_{11}$; in dimension zero there are no coefficients. All statements are local, and at a boundary chart the derivatives are the smooth up-to-boundary coordinate derivatives.

[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],

has dimension three, the restriction of $g_{\gamma(s)}$ to it is positive
definite, and $D_s$ maps normal fields to normal fields, since
$\frac{d}{ds}g(J,T)=g(D_sJ,T)+g(J,D_sT)=g(D_sJ,T)$ and $D_sT=0$; these
facts are proved in [[lem-gr-normal-index-form-factorization]] clause (b).
The norm of a normal field is $|J(s)|:=\sqrt{g_{\gamma(s)}(J(s),J(s))}$.
For any field $V$ along $\gamma$, its **normal component** is the field
$$V^\perp(s):=V(s)+g_{\gamma(s)}(V(s),T(s))\,T(s).$$
Indeed $g(T,T)=-1$ implies $g(V^\perp,T)=0$ and
$V=V^\perp-g(V,T)T$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $R$ be its
curvature ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let
$I,J_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be intervals with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]), and let $F:J_0\times I\to M$ be a smooth map. Write
$T:=\partial_tF$ and $J^F:=\partial_rF$; a field along $F$ means a smooth
section of $F^*TM$ over $J_0\times I$, and $D_r,D_t$ are the covariant
derivatives in the two parameters
([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Curvature as the commutator of the two derivatives.** For every smooth
field $V$ along $F$,
$$\bigl(D_tD_r-D_rD_t\bigr)V=R(T,J^F)V .$$

**(b) Geodesic deviation.** Suppose in addition that for every $r\in J_0$ the
curve $t\mapsto F(r,t)$ is a geodesic with affine parameter $t$, that is
$D_tT=0$. Then $D_tJ^F=D_rT$ and
$$D_t^2J^F=R(T,J^F)T .$$
Consequently, for every $r$ the field $t\mapsto J^F(r,t)$ is a Jacobi field
along the geodesic $t\mapsto F(r,t)$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (b)), and for a geodesic
variation the variation field is a Jacobi field.

**(c) Initial data.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a smooth geodesic and let
$s_0\in I$. For every pair $J_0,J_1\in T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$ there exists exactly
one smooth Jacobi field $J$ along $\gamma$ with
$$J(s_0)=J_0,\qquad D_sJ(s_0)=J_1 .$$
The set of all Jacobi fields along $\gamma$ is a real vector space of
dimension $8$, and $J\mapsto\bigl(J(s_0),D_sJ(s_0)\bigr)$ is a linear
isomorphism onto $T_{\gamma(s_0)}M\oplus T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$.

**(d) The tangential component.** Let $\gamma$ be a smooth geodesic and $J$ a
smooth Jacobi field along it. Then $s\mapsto g(J,\gamma')(s)$ is affine, and
if $\gamma$ is future timelike with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-1$, the normal
component $J^\perp$ of [[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause
(e), explicitly $J^\perp=J+g(J,\gamma')\gamma'$, is again a Jacobi field
along $\gamma$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Then the following
identities hold for all indices $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ and at every point of
every smooth chart:

**(a) Skew-symmetries.** $R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}$ and $R_{abcd}=-R_{abdc}$.
Equivalently, for smooth vector fields,
$$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(X,Y)W,Z\bigr) \quad\text{and}\quad g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(Y,X)Z,W\bigr).$$

**(b) Exchange of the index pairs.** $R_{abcd}=R_{cdab}$, equivalently
$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=g\bigl(R(Z,W)X,Y\bigr)$.

**(c) First Bianchi identity.** $R_{a[bcd]}=0$, that is,
$$R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=0 .$$

**(d) Ricci symmetry.** $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ba}$;
consequently the Einstein tensor is symmetric, $G_{ab}=G_{ba}$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $p\in M$,
let $\mathcal E_p\subseteq T_pM$ be the exponential domain and
$\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$ the exponential map of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]], and identify
$T_{h}(T_pM)$ with $T_pM$ by the canonical isomorphism for every
$h\in T_pM$ ([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]).

**(a) The differential in terms of Jacobi fields.** Let $v\in T_pM$, let
$s_1>0$ satisfy $s_1v\in\mathcal E_p$, and let $u\in T_pM$. Let
$\gamma:[0,s_1]\to M$, $\gamma(t):=\exp_p(tv)$ (well defined by star-shapedness
of $\mathcal E_p$), and let $J_u$ be the unique Jacobi field along
$\gamma$ with $J_u(0)=0$ and $D_tJ_u(0)=u$
([[thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-deviation]] clause (c),
[[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (b)). Then
$$d(\exp_p)_{tv}(tu)=J_u(t)\qquad(0\le t\le s_1);$$
in particular $d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}(s_1u)=J_u(s_1)$ and, in the special case
$s_1=1$, $v\in\mathcal E_p$, $d(\exp_p)_v(u)=J_u(1)$.

**(b) Conjugacy as a kernel condition.** With the notation of (a),
$d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}$ is injective if and only if no nonzero Jacobi field
along $\gamma$ vanishes at $t=0$ and at $t=s_1$. Moreover
$\ker d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}=s_1\{u\in T_pM:J_u(s_1)=0\}$, so
$\dim\ker d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}$ equals the multiplicity of the conjugate
instant $s_1$ whenever $\gamma(s_1)$ is conjugate to $p$ along $\gamma$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (d)).

**(c) Conjugate instants of a geodesic.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a smooth
geodesic with $\gamma(0)=p$, and let $s_1>0$ with $s_1\in I$ and
$s_1\gamma'(0)\in\mathcal E_p$. Then $\gamma(s_1)$ is conjugate to
$\gamma(0)=p$ along $\gamma$ if and only if $d(\exp_p)_{s_1\gamma'(0)}$ is
not injective.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ and the chart $x=\psi_p$ on $T_0M$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

derivations.claim: (The geodesic and its parallel frame.) Along $\gamma$ one has $x^1\equiv\pi/2$, so $\Gamma^1{}_{22}=-\sin(\pi/2)\cos(\pi/2)=0$ and $\Gamma^2{}_{12}=\cot(\pi/2)=0$; by [L1] every Christoffel symbol vanishes along $\gamma$. By [L2], $\nabla_{\partial_2}\partial_2=0$, so $D_sT=0$ and $\gamma$ is a geodesic with affine parameter $s$; likewise $D_s\partial_a=0$ for $a=0,1,2,3$, so the coordinate frame is parallel along $\gamma$ and $D_s$ is the componentwise derivative for fields written in this frame. Finally $g(T,T)=\sin^2(\pi/2)=1$.

(The Jacobi field.) Let $J(s):=\sin(s)\,\partial_1|_{\gamma(s)}$. By step 1.1, $D_sJ=\cos(s)\,\partial_1$ and $D_s^2J=-\sin(s)\,\partial_1$. By [L1] and [L4], $R(T,J)T=\sin(s)\,R(\partial_2,\partial_1)\partial_2=-\sin(s)\,R(\partial_1,\partial_2)\partial_2=-\sin(s)\sin^2(\pi/2)\,\partial_1=-\sin(s)\,\partial_1$. Hence $D_s^2J=R(T,J)T$: $J$ is a Jacobi field by [L3]. It is nonzero (for instance $J(\pi/2)=\partial_1\neq0$) and $J(0)=J(\pi)=0$.

(The general Jacobi field and the first conjugate instant.) Let $K=a\partial_0+b\partial_1+c\partial_2+d\partial_3$ be a smooth field along $\gamma$. By step 1.1, $D_s^2K=a''\partial_0+b''\partial_1+c''\partial_2+d''\partial_3$, while $R(T,K)T=b\,R(\partial_2,\partial_1)\partial_2=-b\,\partial_1$ by [L1] and [L4]: the Jacobi equation is the system $a''=c''=d''=0$, $b''=-b$, with general solution $a=a_0+a_1s$, $b=b_0\cos s+b_1\sin s$, $c=c_0+c_1s$, $d=d_0+d_1s$. If $K(0)=0$ and $K(s_1)=0$ for some $s_1\in(0,\pi)$: the first condition gives $a_0=b_0=c_0=d_0=0$; the second gives $a_1=c_1=d_1=0$ and $b_1\sin s_1=0$, so $b_1=0$ because $\sin s_1\neq0$. Hence $K=0$: no instant in $(0,\pi)$ is conjugate to $0$, and the first conjugate instant of $\gamma$ is $\pi$.

(Conjugacy at $\pi$.) By step 2.1 and [L3], $\pi$ is a conjugate instant of $\gamma$ relative to $0$ with $p=\gamma(0)$ and $\gamma(\pi)=(0,\pi/2,3\pi/2,0)\neq p$: the two distinct points $p$ and $\gamma(\pi)$ of $M$ are conjugate along $\gamma$.

(Multiplicity one and the kernel of the exponential differential.) By step 2.2, a Jacobi field with $K(0)=K(\pi)=0$ has $a_0=b_0=c_0=d_0=a_1=c_1=d_1=0$, hence is $K=b_1\sin s\,\partial_1$: the space of such fields is one-dimensional, so the multiplicity of the conjugate instant $\pi$ is $1$ by [L3]. For the kernel statement, let $v:=T(p)=\partial_2|_p$ and note that the geodesic $\tau\mapsto\exp_p(\tau\pi v)=\gamma(\tau\pi)$ exists for $\tau\in[0,1]$, so $\pi v\in\mathcal E_p$. By [L5], $\ker d(\exp_p)_{\pi v}=\pi\{u\in T_pM:J_u(\pi)=0\}$; solving the system of step 2.2 with initial data $J_u(0)=0$, $D_sJ_u(0)=u$ gives $J_u(s)=u_0s\,\partial_0+u_1\sin s\,\partial_1+u_2s\,\partial_2+u_3s\,\partial_3$ for $u=\sum_au_a\partial_a|_p$, so $J_u(\pi)=0$ if and only if $u_0=u_2=u_3=0$, that is $u\in\mathbb R\,\partial_1|_p$. Hence $\ker d(\exp_p)_{\pi v}=\pi\,\mathbb R\,\partial_1|_p$ is one-dimensional, in agreement with the multiplicity computed above.

boundaries.reason: No indexed family is quantified: the example fixes one metric, one equator geodesic gamma and one Jacobi field J, and computes their properties directly.

No symbolic quotient is formed in the verification: cos and cot are evaluated at x^1 = pi/2 in step 1.1, where cot(pi/2) = 0 is a value rather than a denominator, and the general solution of step 2.2 divides by no function of s.

boundaries.evidence: The multiplicity-one computation is the point of step 4.1: the space of Jacobi fields vanishing at 0 and pi is shown to be exactly the one-dimensional span of sin(s) partial_1, and the kernel of the exponential differential is correspondingly one-dimensional.

Degenerate data are handled: the zero Jacobi field is in the solution space of step 2.2 and is excluded only when nonvanishing is required, and the case in which the two zeros coincide (s1 = 0) is excluded by the interval (0, pi).

Both parameter endpoints are used: J(0) = 0 at the left end and J(pi) = 0 at the right end of the segment, and step 4.1 evaluates the general solution at pi; the events gamma(0) and gamma(pi) are verified distinct in step 3.1, so the endpoint analysis is nondegenerate.

boundaries.reason: The example selects no family: the geodesic and the Jacobi field are given by explicit formulas, and the general solution of step 2.2 is solved in the fixed global coordinate frame.
The example asserts the existence of a conjugate instant and computes its multiplicity; it is not phrased as an equivalence.
No converse sentence is claimed beyond the cited kernel characterization, which is invoked rather than re-proved; step 4.1 closes the computation.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Then the following
identities hold for all indices $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ and at every point of
every smooth chart:

**(a) Skew-symmetries.** $R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}$ and $R_{abcd}=-R_{abdc}$.
Equivalently, for smooth vector fields,
$$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(X,Y)W,Z\bigr) \quad\text{and}\quad g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(Y,X)Z,W\bigr).$$

**(b) Exchange of the index pairs.** $R_{abcd}=R_{cdab}$, equivalently
$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=g\bigl(R(Z,W)X,Y\bigr)$.

**(c) First Bianchi identity.** $R_{a[bcd]}=0$, that is,
$$R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=0 .$$

**(d) Ricci symmetry.** $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ba}$;
consequently the Einstein tensor is symmetric, $G_{ab}=G_{ba}$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $r,s\ge0$ be integers.

**(a) Tensors at a point.** For $p\in M$, the tangent space $T_pM$ is the real
vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]) and the cotangent space is
its algebraic dual, $T_p^*M=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]). A **type
$(r,s)$ tensor at $p$** is a multilinear map

$$T_p:(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\longrightarrow\mathbb R,$$

in the sense of [[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]:
the first $r$ arguments are covectors and the last $s$ are vectors. In
particular a type $(1,0)$ tensor is a vector, a type $(0,1)$ tensor is a
covector and a type $(0,2)$ tensor is a bilinear form, so the covariant
$2$-tensors of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] are exactly the
type $(0,2)$ tensors of this definition.

**(b) The tensor bundle and smooth fields.** The **type $(r,s)$ tensor bundle**
$T^r_sM$ is the disjoint union of the fibres $T^r_sM|_p=\operatorname{Mult}((T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s,\mathbb R)$
over $p\in M$ ([[def-type-r-s-tensor-bundle]]); it carries the smooth
vector-bundle structure defined by the tensor-coordinate change rules
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]). A **smooth
tensor field of type $(r,s)$** on $M$ is a family $T=(T_p)_{p\in M}$ assigning
to each $p$ a type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$, such that for every smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas the **component functions**

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}(q):=T_q\bigl(dx^{a_1}|_q,\dots,dx^{a_r}|_q,\ \partial_{b_1}|_q,\dots,\partial_{b_s}|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$; here the coordinate derivations
$\partial_b|_q=\partial/\partial x^b|_q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]) and the
coordinate differentials $dx^a|_q$ form the dual basis of $T_q^*M$
([[thm-coordinate-differentials-form-the-dual-cotangent-basis]]). This is
equivalent to $T$ being a smooth section of $T^r_sM$ in the sense of
[[def-smooth-tensor-field]]: the component functions are the frame
coefficients of the section in the local frame induced by the chart. The
smoothness condition is independent of the chosen smooth atlas and the
components in two overlapping charts are related by the transformation law
proved in the lemma on this page; the definition is therefore chart
independent rather than merely chart-wise.

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices are written $a,b,c,\dots$ for components in
a chart, with the Einstein summation convention: a repeated index, once upper
and once lower, is summed over $0,1,2,3$. An upper index is a contravariant
slot in which a covector is evaluated, a lower index a covariant slot in which
a vector is evaluated. Slots are moved between these positions with the
musical isomorphisms $\flat_p,\sharp_p$ of
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]; for example, lowering the
first slot of a type $(1,1)$ field uses $(g^\flat T)^a{}_b=g_{ac}T^c{}_b$ and
raising uses $g^{ac}$. This is an identification of slots, not a change of the
field into a field of another kind, and it uses the metric nondegeneracy.

**(d) Scope.** The definition is purely local and chart-based; no global
triviality of $T^r_sM$, no global frame and no choice of metric-compatible
fields is assumed or implied. All fields are smooth ($C^\infty$); no
lower-regularity or distributional tensor field is defined here. The smooth
structure of the tangent bundle, and hence of $T^r_sM$
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]), inherits the
axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] recorded with
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the component formulation of smoothness
itself makes no choice.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $p\in M$. Let
$R_p:(T_pM)^4\to\mathbb R$ be an **algebraic curvature tensor at $p$**: an
$\mathbb R$-multilinear map whose components $R_{abcd}$ in a basis
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]) satisfy
$$R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}=-R_{abdc}=R_{cdab},\qquad R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=0$$
for all $a,b,c,d$. Suppose that for every timelike $T\in T_pM$, every
$J\in T_pM$ and every $W\in T_pM$,
$$R_{abcd}W^aT^bT^cJ^d=0 .$$
Equivalently (by nondegeneracy of $g_p$), the **tidal operator**
$J\mapsto R(T,J)T$ is zero for every timelike $T$, where $R(T,J)T$ is the
vector with $g_p\bigl(R(T,J)T,W\bigr)=R_{abcd}W^aT^bT^cJ^d$ for all $W$. Then
$R_p=0$.

derivations.claim: (The skew-symmetries.) Since $\omega_{ab}=-\omega_{ba}$ for all $a,b$, $T_{abcd}=\omega_{ab}\omega_{cd}=-\omega_{ba}\omega_{cd}=-T_{bacd}$ and $T_{abcd}=-\omega_{ab}\omega_{dc}=-T_{abdc}$: the first two identities of the statement hold everywhere.
(Exchange of the pairs.) Since multiplication of real numbers is commutative, $T_{cdab}=\omega_{cd}\omega_{ab}=\omega_{ab}\omega_{cd}=T_{abcd}$: the third identity holds everywhere.

(The Bianchi sum does not vanish.) For $(a,b,c,d)=(0,1,2,3)$ the sum of the statement is $T_{0123}+T_{0231}+T_{0312}$. The components are $T_{0123}=\omega_{01}\omega_{23}=1\cdot1=1$, $T_{0231}=\omega_{02}\omega_{31}=0\cdot0=0$ and $T_{0312}=\omega_{03}\omega_{12}=0\cdot0=0$. Hence $T_{0123}+T_{0231}+T_{0312}=1\neq0$ at every point of $M$: $T$ violates the first Bianchi identity.

(Conclusion.) Steps 1.1 and 1.2 show that $T$ satisfies the two skew-symmetries and the pair exchange, and step 2.1 shows that it does not satisfy the Bianchi identity. Therefore the displayed statement is refuted: the exchange symmetries alone do not imply the Bianchi identity, which is an independent condition and is imposed separately in the definition of an algebraic curvature tensor [L3]. In particular, by clause (c) of [L1] no metric-selected connection on $M$ has $T$ as its curvature tensor.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $p\in M$. Let
$R_p:(T_pM)^4\to\mathbb R$ be an **algebraic curvature tensor at $p$**: an
$\mathbb R$-multilinear map whose components $R_{abcd}$ in a basis
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]) satisfy
$$R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}=-R_{abdc}=R_{cdab},\qquad R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=0$$
for all $a,b,c,d$. Suppose that for every timelike $T\in T_pM$, every
$J\in T_pM$ and every $W\in T_pM$,
$$R_{abcd}W^aT^bT^cJ^d=0 .$$
Equivalently (by nondegeneracy of $g_p$), the **tidal operator**
$J\mapsto R(T,J)T$ is zero for every timelike $T$, where $R(T,J)T$ is the
vector with $g_p\bigl(R(T,J)T,W\bigr)=R_{abcd}W^aT^bT^cJ^d$ for all $W$. Then
$R_p=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $p\in M$. Let
$R_p:(T_pM)^4\to\mathbb R$ be an **algebraic curvature tensor at $p$**: an
$\mathbb R$-multilinear map whose components $R_{abcd}$ in a basis
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]) satisfy
$$R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}=-R_{abdc}=R_{cdab},\qquad R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=0$$
for all $a,b,c,d$. Suppose that for every timelike $T\in T_pM$, every
$J\in T_pM$ and every $W\in T_pM$,
$$R_{abcd}W^aT^bT^cJ^d=0 .$$
Equivalently (by nondegeneracy of $g_p$), the **tidal operator**
$J\mapsto R(T,J)T$ is zero for every timelike $T$, where $R(T,J)T$ is the
vector with $g_p\bigl(R(T,J)T,W\bigr)=R_{abcd}W^aT^bT^cJ^d$ for all $W$. Then
$R_p=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $r,s\ge0$ be integers.

**(a) Tensors at a point.** For $p\in M$, the tangent space $T_pM$ is the real
vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]) and the cotangent space is
its algebraic dual, $T_p^*M=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]). A **type
$(r,s)$ tensor at $p$** is a multilinear map

$$T_p:(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\longrightarrow\mathbb R,$$

in the sense of [[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]:
the first $r$ arguments are covectors and the last $s$ are vectors. In
particular a type $(1,0)$ tensor is a vector, a type $(0,1)$ tensor is a
covector and a type $(0,2)$ tensor is a bilinear form, so the covariant
$2$-tensors of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] are exactly the
type $(0,2)$ tensors of this definition.

**(b) The tensor bundle and smooth fields.** The **type $(r,s)$ tensor bundle**
$T^r_sM$ is the disjoint union of the fibres $T^r_sM|_p=\operatorname{Mult}((T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s,\mathbb R)$
over $p\in M$ ([[def-type-r-s-tensor-bundle]]); it carries the smooth
vector-bundle structure defined by the tensor-coordinate change rules
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]). A **smooth
tensor field of type $(r,s)$** on $M$ is a family $T=(T_p)_{p\in M}$ assigning
to each $p$ a type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$, such that for every smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas the **component functions**

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}(q):=T_q\bigl(dx^{a_1}|_q,\dots,dx^{a_r}|_q,\ \partial_{b_1}|_q,\dots,\partial_{b_s}|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$; here the coordinate derivations
$\partial_b|_q=\partial/\partial x^b|_q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]) and the
coordinate differentials $dx^a|_q$ form the dual basis of $T_q^*M$
([[thm-coordinate-differentials-form-the-dual-cotangent-basis]]). This is
equivalent to $T$ being a smooth section of $T^r_sM$ in the sense of
[[def-smooth-tensor-field]]: the component functions are the frame
coefficients of the section in the local frame induced by the chart. The
smoothness condition is independent of the chosen smooth atlas and the
components in two overlapping charts are related by the transformation law
proved in the lemma on this page; the definition is therefore chart
independent rather than merely chart-wise.

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices are written $a,b,c,\dots$ for components in
a chart, with the Einstein summation convention: a repeated index, once upper
and once lower, is summed over $0,1,2,3$. An upper index is a contravariant
slot in which a covector is evaluated, a lower index a covariant slot in which
a vector is evaluated. Slots are moved between these positions with the
musical isomorphisms $\flat_p,\sharp_p$ of
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]; for example, lowering the
first slot of a type $(1,1)$ field uses $(g^\flat T)^a{}_b=g_{ac}T^c{}_b$ and
raising uses $g^{ac}$. This is an identification of slots, not a change of the
field into a field of another kind, and it uses the metric nondegeneracy.

**(d) Scope.** The definition is purely local and chart-based; no global
triviality of $T^r_sM$, no global frame and no choice of metric-compatible
fields is assumed or implied. All fields are smooth ($C^\infty$); no
lower-regularity or distributional tensor field is defined here. The smooth
structure of the tangent bundle, and hence of $T^r_sM$
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]), inherits the
axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] recorded with
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the component formulation of smoothness
itself makes no choice.

derivations.claim: (The four algebraic identities.) Since $h_{ab}=h_{ba}$, one has $R_{bacd}=h_{bc}h_{ad}-h_{bd}h_{ac}=-R_{abcd}$ and $R_{abdc}=h_{ad}h_{bc}-h_{ac}h_{bd}=-R_{abcd}$; and $R_{cdab}=h_{ca}h_{db}-h_{cb}h_{da}=h_{ac}h_{bd}-h_{ad}h_{bc}=R_{abcd}$. Moreover $R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=(h_{ac}h_{bd}-h_{ad}h_{bc})+(h_{ad}h_{cb}-h_{ab}h_{cd})+(h_{ab}h_{dc}-h_{ac}h_{db})=0$, each of the three pairs cancelling by $h_{xy}=h_{yx}$. Hence $R$ satisfies the four identities of [L2] at every point.

(The tidal operator vanishes for $T=\partial_0$.) Let $T:=\partial_0$, a future timelike vector with $g(T,T)=-1$. For all $J,W$, by [L1] and the definition of $R$, $g\bigl(R(T,J)T,W\bigr)=R_{abcd}W^aT^cJ^dT^b=R_{a00d}W^aJ^d$ and $R_{a00d}=h_{a0}h_{0d}-h_{ad}h_{00}=0-0=0$, because all components of $h$ with an index $0$ vanish. Hence the pairing vanishes for all $J,W$ and, by nondegeneracy [L1], $R(T,J)T=0$ for every $J\in T_pM$.

(A tilted timelike direction detects the tensor.) Let $T':=\partial_0+\tfrac12\partial_1$; then $g(T',T')=-1+\tfrac14=-\tfrac34<0$, so $T'$ is timelike. Expanding in the constant components, $g\bigl(R(T',\partial_3)T',W\bigr)=R_{abcd}W^aT'^c(\partial_3)^dT'^b=\tfrac14R_{a113}W^a$, with the remaining three terms $R_{a003}$, $R_{a013}$ and $R_{a103}$ vanishing: each of their products contains a factor $h_{0b}$ or $h_{b0}$ for some $b$, and all such components of $h$ are zero. Now $R_{a113}=h_{a1}h_{13}-h_{a3}h_{11}=-h_{a3}$, so $g\bigl(R(T',\partial_3)T',W\bigr)=-\tfrac14W^3$ and, by [L1], $R(T',\partial_3)T'=-\tfrac14\partial_3\neq0$: the tidal operator of $R$ does not vanish for every timelike direction.

(Conclusion.) By steps 1.1 and 1.2, $R$ is a nonzero algebraic curvature tensor; by step 1.3 there is a timelike vector, namely $\partial_0$, for which the tidal operator vanishes identically; by step 2.1 the operator is nonzero for the timelike direction $T'$. Hence the displayed statement is refuted: the vanishing of the tidal operator for a single timelike direction does not force $R=0$, and the hypothesis "for every timelike $T$" in [[lem-gr-algebraic-curvature-vanishing-criterion]] cannot be weakened to a single observer.

boundaries.reason: No family is indexed: the witness fixes one symmetric form h, one tensor R and finitely many directions, and each step evaluates components at a single point.

boundaries.evidence: The zero case is central and is computed rather than assumed away: step 1.3 shows the tidal operator vanishes for T = partial_0 because every component of h with an index 0 is zero, and step 2.1 shows it is nonzero for the tilted timelike direction.

The single-observer hypothesis is exactly the case under attack, and it is realized: step 1.3 exhibits one timelike direction whose whole tidal operator vanishes, so the one-observer case is non-vacuous.

The witness is built from a degenerate symmetric form — h has zero time components and is the Euclidean metric only on the spacelike block — and steps 1.1-1.2 verify that the four algebraic identities still hold for it, which is the degeneracy the example exploits.

boundaries.reason: All objects are constant in the global chart and every statement is pointwise, so no interval endpoint or one-sided limit occurs in steps 1.1-3.1.
The directions partial_0, partial_1 and partial_3 are named explicitly in the coordinate basis, and nothing is selected from a family, so no choice principle is used.
The refuted statement is a one-way implication from single-observer vanishing to R = 0; the witness falsifies that implication, and no forward equivalence is claimed.
No converse statement is being refuted, so the witness supplies no reverse case; step 3.1 collects the falsification.
